newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Twentsche Kabel eyes Chinese expansion.
newsitem.headline: Twentsche Kabel eyes Chinese expansion.

text.p: Dutch cable maker and technical trader NV Twentsche Kabel Holding said on Monday it is studying possibilities to set up cable production in China.
"If you really want to have a share of that market you have to produce there," chairman Harm Smidt told a news conference on Twentsche Kabel's 1996 results.

He said the Chinese cable market is seen growing quickly in the coming years and is expected to reach a total size of about 20 billion guilders by the year 2005. If Twentsche Kabel decides to enter this market it would be with a local partner which knows the country and has the right contacts, Smidt said.
Other areas where Twentsche Kabel plans to expand are Germany, Belgium, France and Britain.

The company expects organic growth and takeovers in its cable manufacturing and technical trading divisions. The machinery making division will grow through joint ventures and because its product range will be widened.

Given Twentsche Kabel's strong balance sheet ratios, with shareholders' equity equalling 58 percent of the balance sheet total, it will be able to buy other firms without having to issue shares unless it is a very large takeover. But Smidt said there were no plans for such large acquisitions right now.

Twentsche Kabel earlier posted a 1996 net profit of 54.3 million guilders, up 14 percent from 1995's 47.6 million. Turnover grew by 91 million guilders to 773 million, including a 60 million rise because of previous takeovers.
For 1997, it expects profits to show a further rise.

The cable making units are seen posting higher turnover but profits will grow here at a somewhat slower pace. In technical trading, turnover and profits are expected to grow and the machinery division will also post higher profits given its well-filled order book, Twentsche Kabel said.
Earlier this year, Twentsche Kabel's share price came under pressure after fellow cable maker NKF issued a warning that it expected profits to fall in 1997.
But Smidt said NKF's situation could not be compared with Twentsche Kabel's as the competitor's problems were mainly caused by its energy cables sector.
At Twentsche Kabel, energy cables generate only 7.5 percent of group turnover and the product mix of the company is quite different to its competitors, Smidt said.
